draft.title: Equivalent fractions and simplest form
card: Equivalent fractions name the same amount. To make one, multiply or divide the top (numerator) and the bottom (denominator) by the same number.
Example: 2/3 = (2×4)/(3×4) = 8/12. Both fractions are the same size, so they are equivalent.
A fraction is in simplest form when the top and bottom share no factor except 1. To get there, divide both by their highest common factor (HCF), the largest number that goes into both.
Example: for 12/18, the HCF of 12 and 18 is 6. So 12/18 = (12÷6)/(18÷6) = 2/3, which is in simplest form.
draft.remember: Do the same thing to the top and bottom. Divide by the HCF to reach simplest form.

a.why: Multiplying top and bottom of 3/5 by 4 gives 12/20. In 6/8 the top is doubled but the bottom has only 3 added, so the fraction changes size.
a.clue: Find the number that turns the 3 and the 5 into the new top and bottom.

b.q: Priya has 24 stickers and 36 of them are shiny. She writes 24/36 as a fraction in simplest form. What does she get?
b.why: The HCF of 24 and 36 is 12, so 24/36 = 2/3. The fractions 4/6, 6/9 and 12/18 are all equivalent to 2/3, but each can still be divided further, so none is in simplest form.
b.clue: Divide by the largest number that goes into both, not just any common factor.

problems.detail: The story is impossible: Priya has 24 stickers but 36 of them are shiny. It should say she has 36 stickers and 24 of them are shiny, so the fraction of shiny stickers is 24/36.

check.summary: The card, question a and both explanations are correct. Question b's story says 36 of Priya's 24 stickers are shiny, which is impossible. Swap it to 36 stickers with 24 shiny.
